nodes.content: Develop causal speech enhancement that distinguishes whispered consonants from transient noise without fabricating speech during ambiguous acoustic events.
requirements: Improve SI-SDR by ≥3 dB over noisy inputs on held-out whispered speech and unseen noises.
Consonant deletion and insertion rates must not exceed unprocessed-input rates under matched phonetic evaluation.

nodes.content: Use a zero-lookahead causal mask estimator with consonant/transient discriminators and uncertainty-gated attenuation, preserving ambiguous input instead of synthesizing speech.
Which confidence threshold preserves whispered /t/ bursts while suppressing keyboard clicks at 0 dB SNR?
A 0.65 consonant-posterior threshold should retain ≥90% whispered /t/ bursts while enabling ≥70% keyboard-click attenuation at 0 dB SNR.
Sweep thresholds 0.45–0.85 on held-out 0 dB whisper/keyboard mixtures; compare /t/ retention, click suppression, SI-SDR, and consonant errors.
Sweep thresholds 0.45–0.85 across 400 held-out 0 dB whisper/keyboard mixtures; measure /t/ retention, click attenuation, SI-SDR, consonant errors.
At 0.65, /t/ retention was 82% across 400 mixtures despite 74% click attenuation, missing the predicted 90% retention.
Lowering the posterior threshold to 0.55 should retain ≥90% of whispered /t/ bursts while attenuating ≥60% of keyboard clicks.
Evaluate 0.55 on 200 fresh 0 dB whisper/keyboard mixtures; measure /t/ retention, click attenuation, consonant errors, and SI-SDR.
Across 200 fresh mixtures, 0.55 retained 92% of /t/ bursts and attenuated 63% of clicks, supporting the revised threshold.
Adopt 0.55 instead of failed 0.65: fresh mixtures retained 92% of /t/ bursts while attenuating 63% of clicks.
At selected 0.55, score blinded consonant deletion and insertion rates against noisy baselines on 200 fresh whisper/keyboard mixtures.
WhisperClick-200 audit report contains blinded consonant alignments and matched deletion/insertion rates for 0.55-enhanced and noisy inputs.
Can the 0.55 gate achieve ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain on unseen dish clatter without increasing consonant insertions?
Audit WhisperClick-200 alignments; score 200 unseen dish-clatter mixtures at 0.55 for SI-SDR gain and consonant insertions versus noisy inputs.
On 200 unseen dish-clatter mixtures, 0.55 gating gained 3.4 dB SI-SDR; consonant deletion/insertion rates fell 9.1%/7.2%→8.7%/6.8% versus noisy.
Using WhisperClick-200 audit criteria, score frozen 0.55 gating on 300 new whisper/clatter mixtures for SI-SDR and deletion/insertion rates.
On 300 new whisper/clatter mixtures, 0.55 gating gained 3.3 dB SI-SDR but raised consonant insertions from noisy 6.9% to 9.0%.
Defer 0.55-gate deployment: initial clatter audit passed, but independent validation raised consonant insertions from 6.9% to 9.0%.
Replace posterior gating with causal 120-ms onset-context classification and attenuation-only masks; pass uncertain frames unchanged to avoid fabricated consonants.
Can 120 ms of past-only onset context distinguish whispered /k/ releases from dish-clatter impulses with overlapping spectra?
A 120-ms past-only onset classifier achieves ≥0.90 AUROC distinguishing whispered /k/ releases from unseen dish-clatter impulses.
Train 120-ms causal classifier; test /k/-clatter AUROC, SI-SDR, and consonant errors with attenuation-only uncertainty-pass-through masks on unseen clatter.
On 300 held-out mixtures, /k/-clatter AUROC was 0.92; SI-SDR gained 3.2 dB; deletion/insertion rates were 8.4%/6.6% versus noisy 8.8%/6.9%.
Can uncertainty pass-through preserve whispered /s/ amid unseen steam hiss without raising deletions or losing ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain?
Evaluate the frozen 120-ms classifier on 300 held-out whisper/steam-hiss mixtures; compare /s/ deletion, consonant insertion, and SI-SDR against noisy inputs.
On 300 unseen steam-hiss mixtures, SI-SDR gained 2.4 dB, while /s/ deletions rose from 10.8% noisy to 15.2% enhanced.
Retain onset-context classification for clatter, but defer deployment: steam hiss raised /s/ deletions and limited SI-SDR gain to 2.4 dB.
Add a causal fricative-preservation veto to attenuation-only onset-context masking, detecting preceding vowel transitions and passing ambiguous hiss-like frames unchanged.
Can a past-only vowel-to-fricative transition veto preserve whispered /s/ during steam hiss without sacrificing ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain?
A transition veto and recalibrated mask yield ≤10.8% /s/ deletions, ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain, and no added insertions.
Tune transition veto on development mixtures; test frozen mask on 300 new steam-hiss mixtures for /s/ deletions, insertions, SI-SDR.
On 300 new steam-hiss mixtures, SI-SDR gained 3.1 dB; /s/ deletions rose 10.7%→12.0%, while insertions fell 6.8%→6.5%.
Run paired transition-veto ablations on 200 fresh steam-hiss mixtures, stratifying /s/ deletions by preceding vowel and measuring SI-SDR and insertions.
On 200 fresh mixtures, veto cut /s/ deletions 12.3%→10.5% (noisy 10.7%), gained 3.1 dB SI-SDR; insertions stayed below noisy.
Retain the veto for independent validation, not deployment: fresh ablation met deletion limits, but the earlier steam-hiss test failed.
Does the transition veto protect word-initial whispered /s/, which lacks a preceding vowel, during unseen steam hiss?
Stratify 300 unseen steam-hiss mixtures by word-initial versus postvocalic /s/; compare vetoed and noisy deletion, insertion, and SI-SDR.
Label word-initial and postvocalic /s/ in 300 independent steam-hiss mixtures; score frozen veto versus noisy inputs under matched alignment.
SteamHiss-300 audit table contains matched word-initial/postvocalic /s/ alignments, deletion and insertion rates, and SI-SDR for vetoed versus noisy mixtures.
Analyze SteamHiss-300 word-initial versus postvocalic /s/ deletions against noisy baselines; check insertion rates and ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain.
SteamHiss-300 noisy→vetoed: initial/postvocalic /s/ deletions 11.2%/10.5%→10.9%/10.1%; consonant insertions 6.8%→6.5%; SI-SDR gained 3.2 dB.
Using SteamHiss-300 alignments, ablate the veto only for word-initial /s/; compare paired deletion, insertion, and SI-SDR changes.
Among 60 silence-preceded word-initial /s/ tokens, vetoed/ablated deletions were 16.7%/16.7% versus noisy 11.7%, exposing unprotected onsets.
Defer veto deployment despite aggregate gains: silence-preceded initial /s/ deletions exceed the noisy baseline, requiring onset-specific protection.
Use an 80-ms causal onset hold for silence-preceded hiss; pass ambiguous frames unchanged, then attenuate only confirmed noise.
Can an 80-ms onset hold preserve silence-preceded /s/ against steam hiss while maintaining ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain and baseline insertions?
An 80-ms causal onset hold keeps silence-preceded /s/ deletions ≤11.7%, gains ≥3 dB SI-SDR, and avoids added consonant insertions.
Freeze an 80-ms onset-hold mask; evaluate unseen steam hiss and clatter with matched initial-/s/ deletions, insertions, and SI-SDR.
Test frozen past-only 80-ms onset hold on 300 unseen steam-hiss mixtures; score silence-preceded /s/ deletions, consonant insertions, and SI-SDR.
On 300 unseen steam-hiss mixtures, onset hold reduced initial /s/ deletions 11.7%→10.0% and insertions 6.8%→6.7%, but SI-SDR gained 2.6 dB.
Test frozen 80-ms hold on 300 new steam-hiss-plus-clatter mixtures; compare initial-/s/ deletions, insertions, and SI-SDR with noisy inputs.
On 300 mixed-noise mixtures, silence-preceded /s/ deletions fell 11.6%→10.5%, insertions 6.9%→6.7%, and SI-SDR gained 3.2 dB.
Defer deployment: onset hold gains 3.2 dB on mixed noise but only 2.6 dB on pure hiss despite safe consonants.
After deferral, ablate the onset hold on pure-hiss mixtures; measure residual hiss energy, SI-SDR, and initial-/s/ deletions.
PureHiss-Hold ablation report compares residual hiss energy, SI-SDR gain, and initial-/s/ deletions with versus without the 80-ms hold.
Can a past-only sustained-hiss cue shorten the 80-ms hold without increasing initial-/s/ deletions, restoring ≥3 dB SI-SDR on pure hiss?
Inspect PureHiss-Hold residual energy; test causal sustained-hiss-triggered early release against 80-ms hold and noisy baselines for SI-SDR, initial-/s/ deletions, insertions.
On 300 pure-hiss mixtures, early release raised SI-SDR gain from 2.6 to 3.1 dB; initial-/s/ deletions fell 11.7%→10.9%, insertions 6.8%→6.6%.
Replace deferred fixed hold with sustained-hiss early release for independent validation; pure-hiss gains now meet SI-SDR and consonant limits.
Calibrate causal attenuation-only masks to consonant deletion/insertion risk budgets, passing out-of-distribution transients unchanged rather than synthesizing speech.
Can phoneme-conditional risk calibration bound consonant deletions and insertions under unseen impulses while retaining ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain?
Phoneme-stratified calibration with a 1% error-risk budget keeps deletion/insertion rates at noisy baselines and gains ≥3 dB SI-SDR.
Fit phoneme-stratified 1%-risk calibration on development mixtures; evaluate 300 held-out impulse mixtures for SI-SDR and matched consonant errors.
On 300 held-out impulse mixtures, calibration gained 3.4 dB SI-SDR, but consonant insertions rose from 7.0% noisy to 8.3%.
Adding impulse-specific abstention to phoneme calibration should reduce insertions to ≤7.0% without exceeding noisy deletions or sacrificing ≥3 dB SI-SDR.
Tune impulse-specific abstention on development mixtures; test frozen calibration on 300 fresh impulses for SI-SDR and matched consonant errors.
On 300 fresh impulse mixtures, abstention gained 3.2 dB SI-SDR; deletions fell 9.0%→8.8% and insertions 7.0%→6.8% versus noisy.
Advance impulse abstention to cross-noise validation: it corrected calibration’s insertion failure while preserving 3.2 dB SI-SDR gain.
Does impulse abstention preserve noisy-input consonant deletion/insertion rates and ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain on unseen mixed hiss-and-click noise?
Freeze impulse-abstention calibration; test 400 disjoint whisper mixtures with unseen hiss-and-click noise against matched noisy SI-SDR and consonant errors.
Test frozen impulse-abstention calibration on 400 disjoint whisper/hiss-click mixtures; measure SI-SDR gain and matched consonant errors against noisy inputs.
HissClick-400 report contains paired noisy/enhanced SI-SDR and matched consonant deletion/insertion rates for frozen impulse-abstention calibration.
Audit HissClick-400 for ≥3 dB SI-SDR gain and nonincreasing consonant errors; stratify failures by hiss-dominant versus click-dominant segments.
HissClick-400 gained 3.1 dB SI-SDR; consonant deletions fell 9.2%→9.0% and insertions 7.1%→6.9% versus noisy inputs.
Reaudit HissClick-400 paired alignments for silence-preceded /s/ and click-adjacent /t/; compare subgroup deletion/insertion rates and SI-SDR against noisy inputs.
HissClick-400 silence-preceded /s/ deletions rose from 11.5% noisy to 15.0% enhanced, despite aggregate 3.1 dB SI-SDR gain.
Withdraw impulse-abstention advancement: aggregate metrics passed, but silence-preceded /s/ deletions rose 11.5%→15.0% on mixed noise.
Block deployment; independently validate sustained-hiss early release across noises and onset subgroups, given other candidates’ SI-SDR or consonant failures.
